business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Alberta applies the English common law tradition within Canada's bijural federal state; the Province of Alberta is not a civil-law jurisdiction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the 1997 and 2007 Protocols
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), 2018
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), 2017
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (double taxation avoidance convention as amended), 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta ULC incorporation: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), s 15.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporation), s 20 (registered office), and regulations thereunder; provincial corporate registry operations: Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registry. AML/CFT: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and PCMLTFA Regulations, enforced by FINTRAC; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.3 et seq. (money-laundering and terrorist-financing offences); economic sanctions: United Nations Act, SC 1999, c 15, Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 31 (Magnitsky Act), administered by Global Affairs Canada; corporate beneficial-ownership transparency: ABCA significant-control register requirements and the federal register of individuals with significant control established under the Canada Business Corporations Act (Corporate Transparency Registry), with government and law-enforcement access; cross-border customs bonding: Customs Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (2nd Supp), administered by the Canada Border Services Agency.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Unlimited Liability Corporation) issued under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) / Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is a Contracting Party effective 11 January 2024; Alberta documents are authenticated by the Alberta Ministry of Justice and Solicitor General; federal documents by Global Affairs Canada). Consular legalization applies only for destination states not party to the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of Articles of Incorporation (ULC designation, share classes, registered office, directors)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta Corporate Registry / corporate counsel issuing certified true copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized incumbency certificate listing directors, officers, and registered shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta notary public or lawyer (Law Society of Alberta)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the individuals-with-significant-control register (UBO disclosure for banking and AML onboarding)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate counsel / company secretary with notarized attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for international banking use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds and financial background dossier of each UBO (AML/CFT record per PCMLTFA, SC 2000, c 17)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where required, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, officer, shareholder, and individual with significant control (including any UBO at or above the 25% statutory threshold) against: (i) the FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) framework, including domestic and foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations as defined under the PCMLTFA Regulations; (ii) the Criminal Code (Canada) listed terrorist entities; (iii) Canadian sanctions lists published by Global Affairs Canada under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, including the Magnitsky Act list; (iv) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (v) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Consolidated Sanctions lists (mandatory for all USD-denominated wire and ACH payment rails); and (vi) supplementary UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists as prudent market practice. Continuous monitoring is required for the life of the relationship; a risk-based re-screening cycle of at least 90 days is recommended for bonded-customs carriers, and all screening results must be retained in accordance with the PCMLTFA five-year record-keeping requirement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registry OnLine / Corporate Registry portal (accessible only through authorized Alberta Registry Agents), using the national NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system; portal URL: https://www.albertacorporateregistry.com/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must be expressed in the Roman alphabet (English or French letters); accents and punctuation are permitted. A ULC incorporated under ABCA s 15.1 must end its name with 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or 'U.L.C.'. Names must be distinguishable and not deceptive in the NUANS national database; any non-Roman trading name must be transliterated into a consistent Roman-script rendering used uniformly in statutory filings, bank documentation, and customs manifests.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires federal Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions consent)
Any term implying federal, provincial, or municipal government patronage or a regulated self-regulatory profession
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written rejection of a proposed name by the Alberta Registrar of Companies, the applicant may (i) within 30 days of the rejection notice, submit to the Registrar a written 'Request for Reconsideration' (administrative appeal) attaching the rejection notice, a fresh NUANS Name Search Report, a legal brief proving distinguishability and non-deception under ABCA s 10, and any ministerial consents or no-objection letters for prohibited tokens; (ii) receive a written Registrar decision; and (iii) if still refused, file an application for judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable statutory appeal window. A 90-day Name Search Report reservation may be renewed before expiry for one further 90-day period at the registry's discretion; if the reservation lapses, a new Name Search Report must be obtained. In practice, filing a new Name Search Report with a revised distinct name is the fastest cure for rejection, while preserving the right of appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Alberta law permits a registered office at a physical address within Alberta at which statutory records may be inspected and process served (ABCA s 20); third-party virtual-office providers are acceptable only if they maintain an actual Alberta street address and licensed registry representation. However, an ISIC 5222 GPS-sealed bonded road-feeder fleet cannot operate with mere virtual substance: the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) requires the corporation to hold and maintain a customs bonded carrier license, a physical dispatcher/terminal facility in Alberta, security bonds, and documented in-transit control procedures under the Customs Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (2nd Supp), Part V. A virtual office is therefore acceptable only as the statutory registered address, not as commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Conservative quantified assessment: (i) 5-15% probability of an unannounced registry or law-enforcement verification visit to the Alberta corporate registered office in any 12-month period; (ii) 60-75% probability of unannounced CBSA bonded-carrier compliance inspections (trailers, GPS seals, cargo documentation, in-transit procedures) during the first 12 months of licensed operation at Calgary International Airport and Edmonton International Airport gateways; (iii) 25-40% annual exposure to Alberta Transportation carrier-enforcement spot audits under provincial highway regulations. The overall unannounced physical inspection likelihood is estimated at 40-60% within the first 24 months of operations, with the highest sensitivity at border crossings and airport cargo facilities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS Pre-Name Search Report (corporate name clearance for Alberta ULC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via authorized Registry Agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory search tariff plus registry-agent processing fee (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Incorporation filing fee — Articles of Incorporation (Unlimited Liability Corporation) under Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, s 15.1
Legal counsel — cross-border ULC structuring, ABCA articles drafting, unanimous shareholder agreement, and unlimited-liability shareholder advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained Alberta corporate counsel / law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Alberta commercial law firms

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, ss 5-6 (incorporation), s 10 (articles), s 15 (registered office), s 17 (name), ss 13-14 (share capital), ss 101-103 (directors), s 160 (records), s 118 (unlimited liability provisions per Part 12 and applicable ULC regulations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta / Corporate Registry System (CORES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form CORES-01) with Memorandum of Association and Notice of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for promissory notes or other valuable consideration as resolved by the sole incorporator and initial director; no mandatory escrow account rule applies for formation, but funds received in trust for share subscriptions must be remitted to the company bank account within 10 business days of deposit; issuance of shares to non-residents permitted without escrow condition under federal Investment Canada Act review thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [ULC NAME], MADE IN WRITING PURSUANT TO THE BUSINESS CORPORATIONS ACT (ALBERTA). RESOLVED: (1) the subscription agreements for common shares are accepted and the issued share register shall record each subscriber, share class, number of shares, and consideration received; (2) the registered office is established at [street address], City of [City], Alberta, and the Registrar is directed to file the Notice of Registered Office; (3) the following individuals are appointed as the first directors and officers: [Name], Chief Executive Officer, [Name], Chief Financial Officer, and [Name], Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting; (4) the banking resolution designating signing officers is approved; and (5) the officers are authorized to execute all filings required for licensing and customs accreditation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized Nuans broker or CORES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request through an Alberta-authorized service provider or directly in CORES to obtain a Name Search Report (NUANS) and a Corporate Name Reservation Certificate. For an unlimited liability corporation, the corporate name must end with 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', or the French equivalent. If the selected name shows conflicting trademarks or corporate names, submit an alternative name or obtain a consent letter from the conflicting entity. The reservation is valid for 90 days and can be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' proposed corporate name and alternative names
Certificate of Authorization if using a name other than in English/French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict, submit a revised name request with supporting consent-letter filing within 30 days, or request a formal administrative review with Corporate Registry; expedited re-search can be processed within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (CORES electronic filing or paper submission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed Form CORES-01, electing the ULC structure under the unlimited liability provisions, including purpose clause, share structure, and director count. File electronically through CORES, or submit two certified paper copies to the Corporate Registry office in Edmonton or Calgary. If filed electronically, use a registry agent account. Pay the registration fee and applicable Nuans fee. The articles take effect on the date certified by the Registrar unless a future effective date is specified.
required_dossiers: Registered Office Information (initial registered office address)
Consent of Proposed Directors (Form with signatures)
Any required amalgamation or continuance documents if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, correct the articles and resubmit within 14 days, or request a Registrar's ruling; adverse decisions are subject to judicial review in the Alberta Court of King's Bench within 30 days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of First Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator acting as sole incorporator, or subsequent board resolution under the ABCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the initial directors are named in the Articles of Incorporation or appointed by written resolution of the incorporator, hold a written First Board Resolution to appoint officers (CEO, CFO, Secretary). Execute the resolution unanimously to adopt Bylaw No. 1, approve share issuance, adopt the share certificate form, appoint auditors or waive audit if permitted by unanimous consent, and approve the initial bank account resolutions. File Form Annual Return within 60 days of incorporation and designate an annual return date.
required_dossiers: Register of Directors and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar notes missing officer or director consents, deliver the signed consents under corporate seal and file a correction; late filing of annual return may incur late filing penalties and loss of good standing, but can be cured within 30 days with late fee payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Corporate Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; registered office physical address must be within Alberta, and records may be held at the registered office or another Alberta location designated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish a registered office in Alberta, which must be a physical street address (P.O. Box not acceptable). File Notice of Change of Registered Office if the address differs from the articles. Prepare and maintain statutory corporate registers: register of directors, register of shareholders, register of transfers, and minute book. Appoint a corporate custodian for statutory records. Ensure written consent of the registered office landlord if the address is provided by a registered agent.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Office Agent or owner
Register of Directors (Form CORES-03 if filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notice of registered office is rejected due to an invalid address, provide corrected address within 10 days; administrative penalty up to CAD 5,000 may be imposed, and the Registrar may dissolve the company for failure to maintain a registered office, but reinstatement can be sought within five years.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Business Number Registration (CRA GST/HST and Payroll)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) online Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, obtain the federal Business Number (BN) via CRA BRO or by mail. Register for GST/HST account (required if gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000, or voluntarily for input tax credits), payroll account if hiring employees, and corporate income tax account. Register for Alberta Provincial Sales Tax not applicable; register for Alberta Corporate Tax account if triggered (low-rate Alberta corporate income tax applies, but ULCs with real estate may have EIFEL implications). Complete any industry-specific registrations such as API fuel account or vehicle licenses for truck fleet.
required_dossiers: Payroll account registration if any employees
Alberta Corporate Tax / ATB account if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the corporate status, provide certified Certificate of Incorporation and Articles; if registration is delayed, telephonic CRA remediation is available, and retroactive effective date can be requested on business need.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Trucking and Customs Bonded Carrier Accreditation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Transport Council / Alberta Transportation Economic Costs and Licensing (if PUC not required for federal); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for Customs Bonded Carrier Licence; Transport Canada FIP for international movements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For customs bonded truck fleet operations, apply to the CBSA for a 'Transportation of Goods by Means of a Customs Bonded Carrier Licence' (Form BSF-540-L / B3-2A). Demonstrate possession of liability and cargo insurance, percent of bonded capability, security bond (typically surety bond for customs obligations), and adherence to the Customs Sufferance Terms and Conditions. If handling air cargo at airport premises, coordinate with airport customs office for a Sufferance Warehouse and Airport In-Bond Trucking agreement. Obtain an Operating Authority (Federal Licence) under the Motor Vehicle Transport Act from Transport Canada / provincial regulatory body for cross-border extra-provincial operations, and IRP (International Registration Plan) plate credentials.
required_dossiers: CBSA Customs Bonded Carrier Licence application (Form BSF-540)
Customs Bond / surety bond with acceptable guarantee amount
Certificate of Incorporation and corporate standing
Certificate of Insurance (auto liability, cargo, environmental)
Commercial vehicle registrations and insurance certificates
National Safety Code (NSC) carrier profile and safety rating
Operating licence from Transport Canada (extra-provincial / FIP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CBSA rejects or conditions the licence, submit a written response to the Customs licensing officer within 30 days addressing deficiencies; failure to maintain bond or insurer certificates can be cured by re-certification and reinstatement request to CBSA Regional Enforcement and Intelligence Division.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Transportation Economic Costs and Licensing (Alberta Transportation), Transport Canada Motor Carrier Licensing, and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Customs Bonded Carrier Licensing Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Canada Border Services Agency Customs Bonded Carrier Licence (Transportation of Goods by Means of Customs Bonded Carrier) and Alberta Commercial Vehicle Operating Licence / Federal Extra-Provincial Operating Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) operating with Environmental Protection Agency-equivalent federal 'Canadian Environmental Assessment Agency' (Impact Assessment Agency of Canada) for restricted activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt — truck fleet operations at existing industrial facilities may require a 'Notification of intention' or 'Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) registration' for fuel storage tanks or/or vehicle maintenance premises but no full EIA report for standard airport feeder operations; full EIA if constructing a new depot, fuel farm, or heavy-duty maintenance workshop exceeding regulatory thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA) for on-road vehicle emissions (ultra-low sulphur diesel, ISO 14001 voluntary fuel management); Alberta environmental air quality release limits under the 'Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives'; wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must conform to municipality sewer-use bylaws (e.g., oil-water separator with performance of 15 ppm total oil and grease before discharge); VOC and petroleum storage tank supervision under EPEA AEP storage tank regulation — secondary containment (double-wall tanks or containment dike) required for above-ground fuel storage; waste handling per Technical Guidance on PCB, solvent waste, and used oil regulations; hazardous waste manifest under the EPEA Waste Control Regulation

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: obtain a 'Fire Safety Inspection Certificate' from the Alberta Fire Commissioner / municipal fire department for the terminal depot and vehicle maintenance areas, including fuel storage license and fire extinguisher inspection; structural load inspection certified by a licensed structural engineer for office and maintenance bay floors to verify axle lift capacities and heavy-duty vehicle access; workplace clearance: provide employer Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) certification, Occupational Health and Safety Code compliance under the Alberta OHS Act (maintenance pits, forklift charging station, and hazardous goods handling), and proof of workplace inspection by Alberta Labour OHS officer for vehicles lifting areas and where dangerous goods are handled; possession of fire suppression permits for any on-site fueling station.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via its My Business Account portal at canada.ca/revenue-agency
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities such as Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporations obtain their Business Number (BN) automatically upon registration with the Alberta Corporate Registry, which integrates with CRA systems. Foreign entities seeking to operate in Canada must apply for a BN by submitting Form RC59 or equivalent to the CRA, including incorporation documents and business details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or similar elections available under Canadian tax law. Taxation follows the legal entity structure, with ULCs classified as corporations subject to entity-level taxation unless restructured as a partnership.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 in annual taxable supplies of goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns through CRA's My Account system. Businesses must maintain digital records and may be required to provide real-time data under certain compliance programs, though full real-time clearance is not standard for all.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST rate applies to exports of goods from Canada or services performed outside Canada. For a customs bonded truck fleet, this includes international road transport services and goods movement qualifying as exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may scrutinize zero-rated transactions. Fraudulent claims result in penalties of up to 200% of the evaded tax, plus interest, and potential criminal charges with retrospective tax adjustments and clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority, LVTS oversight, and Retail Payment Activities Act registration); FINTRAC (AML/CFT and international wire/cross-border transaction reporting); OSFI (prudential supervision of bank FX risk). Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration at the federal level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada observes IMF Article VIII full current and capital account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is freely floating and internationally accepted. No foreign-exchange approval is required for equity injections, trade settlements, debt servicing, or profit remittances by an Alberta ULC. Dividend distributions to non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, potentially reduced by tax treaty, but are not blocked or licensed by any foreign-exchange authority. Non-Canadian investors establishing or acquiring a Canadian business should also verify the Investment Canada Act notification/review obligation; this is an investment-screening requirement, not a currency-control restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada does not impose statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory repatriation timelines, or minimum conversion ratios. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the client's discretion. Financial institutions must report completed international electronic funds transfers (IEFTs) and large cash/currency transactions of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and must maintain underlying trade documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and FX Settlement Account
Operational Account and Customs-Bonded Operating Reserve

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail; Medium/Low as an ancillary payout rail. An offshore fintech or electronic money institution is not an authorized deposit-taking institution under the Canadian Bank Act and cannot provide LVTS or Canadian clearing access. Such an EMI may operate in Canada only if registered with FINTRAC as a money services business and, where applicable, recognized under the Retail Payment Activities Act (administered by the Bank of Canada). The ULC should use a Schedule I Canadian bank as the master clearing counterparty; an EMI may serve only as a supplementary payment channel for niche cross-border payouts, with balances maintained at very low levels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute requires every director to appear physically. For foreign-owned ULCs, Canadian banks will require at least one authorized signing officer or ultimate beneficial owner to complete a certified identity verification. In-person branch attendance is commonly required when the corporate structure is non-standard or when the bank cannot validate foreign ownership records electronically. Remote opening is possible but normally conditioned on video verification, notarized corporate documents, a Canadian registered office/agent, and a Canadian-director or authorized representative with signing authority. The ULC should expect enhanced due diligence interviews for its shareholder(s), the unlimited-liability structure, and the customs-bonded revenue stream.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-owned ULC with unlimited shareholder liability and pass-through eligibility creates ambiguity on beneficial ownership and corporate separateness.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; ULC operating agreement/articles; register of directors and shareholders; ultimate beneficial owner declarations with percentage ownership; notarized passports and residential proof for all 10%+ owners; external legal opinion explaining ULC liability and tax pass-through election; power of attorney/authorized signatory certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs-bonded trucking and airport feeder operations involve cross-border freight payments to third-party carriers, fuel vendors, customs brokers, and airport authorities, creating source-of-funds traceability concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBSA bonded carrier license or equivalent customs authorization; customs bond surety documents; GPS-seal integrity reports; executed road feeder service agreements with airlines/forwarders; client invoices and settlement statements; terminal handling agreements; driver/cargo manifests; board resolution describing the trade-flow and payment chain; names and business numbers of all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value disbursements for truck/trailer acquisition, fuel-card accounts, and cross-border insurance may trigger bank limits or unexplained-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quotes and pro-forma invoices for fleet assets; equipment lease/financing agreements; fuel-card master agreements; insurance policies; source of wealth documentation for shareholder funds; audited or internally prepared financial statements; CRA business number confirmation; current Alberta corporate registry report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or receipt from countries adjacent to or outside Canada with elevated sanctions risk may be detected in SWIFT screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions screening policy; denied-party screening results; country-of-origin and country-of-destination matrix; letters from customers confirming no embargoed goods; customs entry/bond records; CBSA release documents; board-approved trade-compliance manual; OFAC/CBSA/UN sanctions self-certifications.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound shareholder equity or shareholder-loan proceeds using SWIFT MT103 from the foreign corporate bank to the ULC's Schedule I Canadian bank account. The wire narrative must state 'ULC equity contribution' or 'ULC shareholder loan' and include the ULC legal name, Canadian bank account number, and unique reference. USD funds may be retained in a USD operating account or converted to CAD at the bank's spot rate; no Canadian exchange-control permit is required. The bank will complete FINTRAC international electronic-funds-transfer reporting at C$10,000 or above. For non-Canadian shareholders, verify whether Investment Canada Act initial notification is required; retain board resolutions, subscription agreements, loan agreements, source-of-funds statements, and the bank's inward transfer advice in the treasury file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border wire payments to suppliers, subcontracted truckers, fuel providers, and customs brokers; use MT202 COV for bank-to-bank cover where intermediary banks are involved. For Canadian-dollar domestic disbursements, use Payments Canada ACSS/ACH for recurring payroll/fuel-card top-ups and LVTS wires for high-value transactions. For large fleet/trailer purchases requiring payment assurance, use a commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700/MT707. Maintain trade-payment evidence in the form of commercial invoices, customs entries, bills of lading, Cargo Reports, GPS-seal logs, and terminal handling receipts. For US-dollar settlements, clear via the bank's US correspondent through Fedwire or CHIPS; ACH Direct can be used for recurring lower-value USD payables.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD FX forwards executed with a Schedule I Canadian bank under an ISDA/Canadian Master Agreement
USD/CAD OTC cross-currency swaps for matching hard-currency revenue with foreign-currency liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid/non-convertible third-market currencies where the bank can lawfully offer NDF pricing
European-style FX options for hedging projected USD-denominated airline and cargo revenue without speculative leverage
USD/CAD spot/forward rolling hedges for monthly customs-bonded settlement cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporate Registry annual return (annual declaration under Corporations Information Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta – Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing creates registry-default status and late-fee exposure; continued failure for one year past the due date supports administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Registrar, which terminates the ULC's legal capacity to operate the customs bonded truck fleet.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including Alberta corporate tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Calgary Tax Centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, plus prescribed interest; chronic defaults expose directors to personal liability for unremitted amounts and allow CRA collection actions against fleet assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return under the annual-filer election
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST filers; quarterly filers follow the standard quarterly due dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and prescribed interest apply under the Excise Tax Act; repeated default can lead to garnishment of receivables, seizure of bonded cargo assets, and loss of CRA clearance required for customs bonding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Customs Bonded Truck Carrier authorization status and indemnity bond continuity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) – Commercial Registration Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance with no lapse; CBSA validates bond continuity and authorization status at each carrier anniversary or upon any change in corporate identity, control, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the indemnity bond or loss of valid corporate standing results in suspension or cancellation of the bonded truck authorization, exposure to unpaid duties, and potential seizure of released customs documents and goods under the Customs Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-only financial test governs a non-distributing Alberta ULC. An independent auditor must be appointed unless the ULC is validly exempted by unanimous shareholder resolution; audit is mandatory for distributing corporations and may be required by CRA, CBSA, or the customs-bond surety as a condition of bonding.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for public or distributing entities; a private Alberta ULC engaged in customs bonded trucking may prepare statutory financial statements under Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Part II) as local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta registries do not require a separate filed UBO annual return for a private ULC. The ULC must maintain a current Register of Individuals with Significant Control at its registered office and enter any transfer or change in significant control within 15 days of becoming aware. The annual return filed with Alberta Corporate Registry confirms registered office, directors, and corporate standing but does not require ownership schedules; the significant-control register must be produced on demand to the Registrar or enforcement authority.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180-450 per year for Alberta registered office and registered agent services for a private ULC.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-15,000 per year for a small-to-mid-sized Alberta customs bonded truck fleet ULC where intercompany bonded transactions and CBSA financial-review requirements affect audit complexity.
